digest.component_or_area: Cloud adapter (Jira) - resilience and configuration validation coverage parity with DC
propositions: Cloud's per-member 429 retry behavior is split across four distinct layers (direct REST, ACLI subprocess, dispatch wrapper, non-retrying apply phases) with opposite retry semantics, and every mutating transport member must be explicitly enumerated and classified on both axes (transport seam and dispatch level) with duplicate-write safety assessed for known deliberate retries.

Cloud lacks config-validation coverage for non-HTTPS base URLs, missing credentials, and hardcoded resolved-status sets that DC has gained, requiring tests to document either rejection behavior or deliberate absence with follow-up bugs for silent failures.

Cloud's probe resolves workflow status states via a hardcoded frozenset (Resolved, Done, Cancelled) while DC threads resolved_statuses from runtime config, requiring a decision on whether Cloud deployments with non-standard workflow states need a runtime config hook or can work with per-deployment constants.

DC provides no user-search methods matching Cloud's three aliases, so user-search bootstrap degrades to string matching on DC rather than raising, requiring an explicit pin that the degradation is correct.

Cloud bypasses its own retry wrapper in multiple paths including bare urllib.request.urlopen calls, creating risk that mutations inherit undocumented retries or lack documented retries depending on which dispatch boundary they traverse.

Each 429 sweep must assert actual attempt count per seam (one attempt for non-retrying layers, bounded Retry-After backoff for subprocess, bounded retry for dispatch wrapper) with mutation-checked test coverage demonstrating the assertions fail when retry behavior is removed.
